clue.text: Express unhappiness when hard American soldiers turn up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone groans when tough US troops arrive on the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses H + GIS, the whole run read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh is to breathe out audibly as a sign of sadness or weariness.

clue.text: Mark wants nothing less than Hollywood's highest honour!

indicators.note: less means the letter for nothing is taken away from the award's name

parts.note: the Oscar is the top film award given in Hollywood
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A film-maker wants nothing short of an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O (nothing) from OSCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting blemish left on skin, a kind of mark.

clue.text: Some rather big leaves used by the cook

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook uses some fairly large leaves in a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Culinary herbs such as basil and bay are leaves used to flavour food.

clue.text: The horse carrying a large figure appeared overheated

indicators.note: a horse carrying something holds it, so these letters go inside the word for the horse

parts.note: a steed is a horse, especially a spirited riding horse
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a large figure

explanation.surface: A horse bearing a heavy rider looked hot and sweaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts A + M inside STEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steamed gives off vapour, as a hot, sweating body does after exertion.

clue.text: A man dropped will naturally be dejected

parts.note: a chap is a man
fallen means dropped, come down

explanation.surface: A fellow who has been let go will understandably feel down.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapfallen is an old word for downcast, literally with the jaw hanging slack.

clue.text: For a marksman of the old school?

definitions.text: For a marksman of the old school?

parts.words: For a marksman of the old school?
parts.note: two readings: a rifle a sharpshooter of former days might carry, and a boy from one of England's oldest public schools

explanation.surface: Something suited to a sharpshooter of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: WINCHESTER is both a famous repeating rifle and Winchester College, one of England's oldest fee-paying schools, so 'old school' also points at a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A Winchester is a classic lever-action rifle, and Winchester College is an ancient English school.

clue.text: Most important, and correspondingly rubricated?

explanation.surface: Something both vital and, fittingly, marked in red.
explanation.walkthrough: Important feast days were printed in red in church calendars, hence a red-letter day; to rubricate is to mark in red.
explanation.definitionFit: Special days were picked out in red ink in calendars, so the term means both memorable and literally written in crimson.

clue.text: Article about a fellow causing distress

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
c, short for circa, means about
he refers to a male, a fellow

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about some man has caused upset.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull persistent pain, a form of suffering.

clue.text: A swimmer having a fling — he's going wild

indicators.note: going wild says the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: he's is he is, giving its three letters

explanation.surface: A swimmer having a wild affair has lost control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going wild' rearranges AFLINGHES; the def 'A swimmer' uses the first A, the fodder the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The angelfish is a brightly coloured tropical fish, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Useful material and the way the swine put inside had to obtain it

indicators.note: put inside says the way and the swine both go within the following word

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
a boar is a male pig, a swine

explanation.surface: A recipe for getting building board involving roads and pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the swine' looks like an insult for the person; it is just a pig. 'put inside' sends both the road and the pig into the word had.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardboard is stiff compressed fibreboard, a handy sheet stuff for building and crafts.

clue.text: Note the old-fashioned colour

parts.note: D is a musical note
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: Note the quaint shade of this fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ye olde' shop signs use YE for THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dye is a substance used to stain or tint, giving a hue.

clue.text: Part written page perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be put in another order

explanation.surface: A partly written sheet, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PAGE; 'Part' is a verb here, as lips part.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open wide or split apart, as a mouth or wound does.

clue.text: Don't stand for such blatant deception

explanation.surface: Refuse to put up with such barefaced dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand for' looks like tolerate, but 'Don't stand' is one sense: lie down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie is to recline rather than be upright, and a lie is an untruth.

clue.text: Watch pet mice scampering about — that is the answer

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the jumble goes round the short letters
mice scampering about run in all directions, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on pet mice running around; there lies the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scampering' jumbles the seven letters of 'pet mice', and 'about' wraps that jumble round 'that is'; 'the answer' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a small portable clock, a device for telling time.

clue.text: A spread for the board

parts.note: board is the dining table, and spread is something laid over it rather than a feast

explanation.surface: A feast laid on for the directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' suggests a meal and 'board' a company's directors; read literally it is a covering laid on a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablecloth is a cover spread over a dining table, a board in the old sense.

clue.text: This may well be understood at Christmas!

definitions.text: This may well be understood at Christmas!

parts.words: This may well be understood at Christmas!
parts.note: understood is read as stood under: couples stand beneath this festive plant to kiss

explanation.surface: Something easily grasped during the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understood' splits as 'under-stood': people kiss standing beneath this sprig at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistletoe is the white-berried plant hung up at Christmas for kissing beneath.

clue.text: Country people getting head start in game

indicators.note: getting the letter in means the rural folk take it inside

parts.note: peasants are rural farming people

indicators.note: start means only the first letter of head is used

explanation.surface: Rural folk gain an early lead in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes H from 'head', and 'getting ... in' places it inside PEASANTS; 'game' means birds shot for sport, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants are birds shot for sport and food, classic examples of game.

clue.text: Heavy metal star

explanation.surface: A rock music celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' poses as rock music; it is the dense element Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense grey element, and the lead is the principal performer in a show.

clue.text: The girl in a dissolute situation can get embarrassed

indicators.note: in places the girl's pronoun within the other letters

parts.note: bad here means wicked or dissolute
she refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman caught in a debauched setting may feel mortified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the pronoun for the girl inside 'a' plus the word for dissolute; 'situation' and 'can get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashed means made to feel ashamed or self-conscious.

clue.text: Gravely in need of help (money) in a beastly home

indicators.note: in a beastly home places help and money within the animal's pen

parts.note: a sty is a home for pigs, beasts
aid means help
L stands for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Seriously needing assistance and cash while living in a pigpen.
explanation.walkthrough: L is from Latin libra, the pound sign, so it can stand for money; 'in need of' is a link, and 'in a' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Staidly means in a sober, serious, sedate manner.

clue.text: Badly crushed? There's a doctor round the corner

indicators.note: round says the doctor's letters go around the corner word

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, means a doctor
an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: Someone has been hurt, but medical help is just nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the doctor's letters around the corner; 'There's' is a link. The surface suggests a doctor nearby, but 'round the corner' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangled means mutilated or damaged by crushing or tearing.

clue.text: Pine for old port

explanation.surface: Long for a harbour of former days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb, long; it is pine wood. Deal is a town in Kent, once one of the Cinque Ports.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn pine or fir timber, and Deal is a historic Kentish seaport.

clue.text: Chain-user — nasty prickly little creature

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who uses a chain is a horrible spiky little brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges CHAINUSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a small marine animal covered in spines.

clue.text: Companies kept short of salad stuff

indicators.note: kept short means the word for firms is cut down to its standard abbreviated form

parts.note: the word companies taken as written before it is abbreviated

explanation.surface: Firms reduced their supply of salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept short' cuts the middle out of 'Companies', leaving the usual abbreviation; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of long-leaved lettuce, a salad green.

clue.text: A woman of character with a following

indicators.note: following says the second letter comes after the character's name

parts.note: en is the spelt name of the letter N, a character

explanation.surface: A lady of note who has many admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts A after EN. Ena Sharples was a well-known character in the British soap Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Ena is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Boring bit of stage-setting

explanation.surface: A dull piece of theatre scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means dull and lifeless, and a flat is a painted scenery panel on stage.

clue.text: Place of entertainment offering varied things to have a shot at

indicators.note: varied means the letters are changed around

parts.note: to pot is to take a shot at, as with a gun

explanation.surface: A fairground stall offering assorted prizes to aim at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges THINGS to NIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub or bar, a venue for evening amusement.

clue.text: Drinks for children

explanation.surface: Beverages meant for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link: tots are small measures of spirits and small children.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small dram of liquor, and tots are toddlers.

clue.text: Flower worn by a huntsman

explanation.surface: A bloom pinned on a fox-hunter's lapel.
explanation.walkthrough: In British fox-hunting the scarlet coat is called hunting pink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are clove-scented garden blooms, and a hunting coat is traditionally called pink.

clue.text: Can't find shade

parts.note: a can is a tin
the apostrophe-t contributes its letter

explanation.surface: Unable to locate some shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't' is split as Can + 't; 'find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a hue or gradation of colour.

clue.text: A viewer's complaint

parts.note: the viewer is an eye, and the complaint is an ailment rather than a grumble to a broadcaster

explanation.surface: A TV watcher writes in to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewer' suggests a TV watcher and 'complaint' a grievance; it means an eye ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an eye ailment.

clue.text: Give voice about small number adding sugar

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the singing word goes round the rest

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
wee is Scottish for small
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Sing about a little figure while sugaring tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the singing word round the small word and the number; 'Give voice' looks like the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetening means making something sweeter, as by stirring in a sweetener.
